title: Dental Specialty Clinic · MOH 4Ps
description: Dental specialty clinic inspection checklist · Ministry of Health 4Ps

items.text: The dental specialty clinic shall be directed by licensed dental surgeon.
The dental specialty clinic shall provide service at outpatient/ambulatory level only.
Emergency care specific to dentistry with qualified staff available during working hours.
Continuous quality improvement program for services.
Display visible notices: Services list, Professionals list, Fees and prices list.
Facilities well marked and easily accessible for persons with disability.
Running water supply & functional hand washing basin in all patient care rooms.
Functional access mechanism (stairs/ramp or stairs/elevator) for multi-floor units.
Established system for verbal and written communication about patient care.
Number and type of technical staff determined by workload analysis.
Dental surgeon (DDM) shall not perform removable complete denture, fixed complete denture, and maxillofacial prosthodontics (reserved for advanced specialists).
Provide ambulatory care, follow-up, preventive, health promotion, and chronic illness care.
Comprehensive patient assessment (history, physical exam, vital signs, clinical exam, diagnostics, lab/imaging).
Fully describe treatment options to client/family and document in medical record.
Medical records complete regarding history, exam, oral examination, diagnosis, procedures, medications, and treatment.
Nurse takes vital signs and necessary assessments prior to dental service.
Dental service provided in accordance with infection prevention standards.
Functional referral system (urgent conditions, SOPs, direct referral, directory, forms, tracing, feedback, documentation).
Outpatient service well marked and easily accessible for disabled, elderly, children, and pregnant women.
Patient waiting area and corridor ventilated and child-friendly.
Adequate light, ventilation, and privacy in all outpatient rooms.
IEC and entertaining materials available in waiting area.
Reception, Recording & Waiting area for oral health education
Examination and treatment room with dental unit
Dental x-ray room (optional if integrated with dental unit)
Burnisher (ball type, football type, interproximal type) (optional)
Light curing unit with composite materials
Kit for friction lock retention pin
Matrix band and retainer (metallic & celluloid, different sizes)
Materials & instruments to keep area free from moisture & improve visibility
Micro motor with hand piece and burs
Forceps for Dental Extractions (Deciduous & Permanent teeth)
Impression Trays for upper & lower jaws
Preformed temporary stainless steel & polycarbonate crowns
Arch wires (Niti & Stainless steel in various dimensions)
Mandrels, Carborundum, Silica, Crocus discs and stones
Local anesthesia (Spray, Lidocaine multi-dose, Cartridges with/without adrenaline)
Medical record maintained in written form for every patient seen.
Individual medical records maintained to ensure accuracy and easy retrieval.
Written policy/procedure for record completion, release of info, and protection against loss/tampering.
Medical records kept confidential and available only to authorized persons.
Entries written legibly in permanent ink, dated, and signed.
Required record contents (ID, history, exam, diagnosis, meds, procedures, notes, provider signature, signed consent form).
Consent forms printed in understandable format with non-technical language.
Mechanism for controlling and tracing medical records in/out of central records room.
Mechanism to make appointment records ready and return seen cards within 24 hours.
Medical certificates and copies documented on original medical record.
Procedure for removal of inactive medical records from central room.
Medical records destroyed as per law ensuring confidentiality (records active for >10 years preserved).
Medical record room premises suitable for movement, shelved properly (3-4 inches off floor/walls).
Medical record room has adequate space (central filing, workspace, archive, supply storage).
Medical record room built far from fire and damaging sources.
Dedicated room/area for archiving dead files.
Full-time custodian / Health Information Technician with basic computer skills.
Basic training on medical record keeping provided to staff.
Minimum medical record equipment (shelves, MPI boxes, computer/printer, reporting formats, cart, ladder, folders, MPI cards, logbook, fire extinguisher).
Health promotion service available in dental clinic.
Plan, schedule, coordinate, lead and monitor clinic-specific health promotion activities.
Respect national health policy, legislation, protocols and directives.
Designated health professional to coordinate health promotion activities.
Waiting area at reception with audiovisual health promotion materials.
Technical manager leads identification of priority conditions and prep of materials.
Roles and responsibilities specified in job description.
Health professionals provide health education in their discipline.
Audiovisual and printed materials (TV, DVD/VCD, Radio, Tape-recorded) at reception.
All activities comply with national infection prevention and control guidelines.
IPC effectively and efficiently governed and managed.
Identify infection risk procedures and implement reduction strategies (PPE, cleaning, sterilization, isolation, waste disposal, aseptic technique).
Provide IPC training for all staff as per national guidelines.
Maintain decontamination, reprocessing, environmental cleaning, waste management, hand hygiene, PPE, and sharp safety.
Train staff on minimizing exposure to blood-borne infections (first aid, reporting, PEP program evaluation).
Basic or refresher training on IPC for staff at least once per year.
Infectious and non-infectious medical wastes handled, segregated (3-bin system), and treated (incineration, autoclaving, chemical/steam sterilization).
Clean and safe environment, continuous safe water supply.
Routine cleaning and sanitizing of patient areas and waiting rooms at least twice daily.
Functional sewerage system with flushing toilets.
Housekeeping and maintenance services (cleaning protocols, odor control, equipment maintenance, fire/emergency preparedness, backup power).

title: Medium Private Clinic
description: Medium private clinic inspection / supervision checklist

items.text: The medium clinic shall be directed by a General Practitioner / Public Health Officer / BSc Nurse / BSc Midwife.
The clinic shall provide service only at outpatient/ambulatory level at least during working hours.
Emergency care with qualified staff shall be available during government working hours.
The medium clinic shall avail updated reference materials, treatment guidelines, and manuals for common diseases.
Diseases under national surveillance shall be notified to the FMOH through the proper reporting channel.
The medium clinic shall have at a minimum the required health personnel and support staff (see detailed table below).
The medium clinic shall conduct workload analysis.
The medium clinic shall assign a quality focal person to improve quality of service deliveries.
The medium clinic shall provide or facilitate training to their staff.

The medium clinic shall display in a visible place: / a) List of available services (during & after working hours) / b) List of working professionals (during & after working hours) / c) Updated list of various fees and prices
The medium clinic facilities shall be well marked and easily accessible for persons with disability.
Potential sources of accidents shall be identified and acted upon (slippery floors, doorways, footsteps).
All patient care rooms shall be provided functional hand washing basin.
Internal surfaces (floors, walls, ceilings) shall be: / a) Smooth, impervious, free from cracks / b) Easy to clean and decontaminate / c) Non-combustible / fire-resistant
Circulation ways and sub-corridors shall be a minimum 2m wide.
Patient serving corridors shall not be less than 2m wide.
Glass doors shall be marked to avoid accidental collision.
Multi-floor facilities shall have horizontal/vertical access mechanism (stairs & ramp or stairs & elevator).
MCH room with or without obstetric ultrasound
Shower room and toilet (if delivery service available)
Duty room (if emergency service is 24 hours)
Patient dressing cubicle inside X-ray room
Area for placenta pit (if delivery service available)
Doctor of Physiotherapy (DPT) or Physiotherapy Specialist (MSc) or Physiotherapy Professional (BSc)
Physio ball (one big and one small size)
Cotton rolls, POP, gauze bandage, POP scissors

Prosthesis & Orthotics Workshop tools: Oven, Bench vice, Leather sewing machine, Tool case, Vacuum pump, Scissor, Grinder stand, Hack saw, Suction (dust aspirator), Drill conical, Bench Drill, Riveting bar, Jig saw, Safety equipment, Saw oscillating (cast cutter), Glove (PU coated), Heat gun, Sand drum, Welding Iron, Contouring instrument (Bender), Welding mirror, Revolving Hole puncher, Measuring tape, Caliper gauge, Rivet setter

Consumables for Prosthesis & Orthotics: EVA, Indelible pencil, Homopolymer (PP), Plaster mixing bowl, Gypsum Powder, Velcro, Stanley surform, Glue, Sewing needles, Foot (different size), Ring half round (D-Ring), Module system, Knife (cutter), Ankle/Knee/Hip joint, Rivet tubular iron, Side bar, Copper rivet, Cotton stockinet, Sand paper, Cast cutter blade, Jig saw blade, Hack saw blade, Drill bit
Tap water / water container with faucet

title: Primary Clinic
description: Private primary clinic inspection / supervision checklist

items.text: The primary clinic shall have a minimum of the following premises set up (see details below).
The Primary clinic shall have direct access to examination room for emergency.
The Primary clinic shall have hand washing basin/ facility at examination and treatment room.
There shall be a note in visually accessible area that details the facilities working hours and list of services available.
The primary clinic shall have the required staffing (see details below).
The primary clinic shall have adequate supplies and equipment needed for IPC practice.
Infectious and medical wastes shall be handled and managed according to recent guidelines.
Segregation of health care waste (separate types, colored receptacles, at source, 3-bin system).
The clinic shall have a medical waste management plan (storage, segregation, transport, disposal).
Supportive sanitation measures (clean water, hand hygiene, sterilization, PPE alternatives).
Sanitary system (flushing toilets, plumbing stores, sanitary office, incinerator, pits, secured solid waste area).
The primary clinic shall officially designate staff in charge of handling waste on a regular basis.
Equipment and supplies required for sanitation activities (Incinerator, safety boxes, leak-proof containers, trolley, PPE, autoclave, pressure cooker, cleaning solutions, mops and dustbins).
The ophthalmology specialty clinic shall provide ophthalmology services at outpatient level only at least during regular working hours.

The medical assessment for eye shall include at least: / a) Comprehensive medical and social history, / b) Physical examination for ophthalmology including at least visual acuity, vital signs (BP), clinical exam pertinent to illness, slit lamp/fundo-ophthalmoscope exam, / c) Diagnostic impressions, / d) Visual Field test, / e) Intra ocular pressure (IOP)/Tonometry, / f) Keratometry and ultrasound (optional).
There shall be minor surgical procedures with local and regional anesthesia as stated by minor surgical standards of this document.
There shall be optometry service available in the clinic.
The Ophthalmology Service shall be provided by a licensed ophthalmologist.
The clinic shall have client medical records, registers and reporting formats as per the national system.
The ophthalmology/Eye clinic shall have rooms (outpatient service areas) as specified below (see detailed breakdown).
A Corridor with a minimum of 6m long for visual acuity examination.
All rooms shall have washing basin with running water.
Procedure/minor surgery room with Scrub room
Observation room with 2 couches for observation
The eye clinic shall be directed by licensed ophthalmologist with two years of relevant clinical experience available at all working hours.
The nurse practicing in eye clinic shall be trained and experienced on ophthalmology services.
The eye clinic shall have the minimum staffing (Ophthalmologist #1, Nurse #1, Optometrist/Refractionist #1 conditional, Receptionist #1, Cleaner #1).
The eye clinic shall have the required equipment, diagnostic medicines, supplies, and consumables (see detailed breakdown below).
Trial set with trial frame (children and adult)
Probing set / Lacrimal dilator and probe
